title: Korean-Style Marinated Grilled Beef with Lettuce Wraps
summary: Paper-thin beef soaks in a pear, garlic and soy marinade, then sears in a very hot pan and is served in lettuce wraps with rice and a punchy chilli dipping sauce.
equipment: large cast-iron frying pan or grill pan

ingredients.item: rib-eye or sirloin steak, fat trimmed
small Asian or ripe Conference pear, peeled, cored and chopped (about 150 g)

ingredients.note: check the label: some soy sauces list alcohol

ingredients.item: spring onions, cut into 3 cm lengths, plus 1 thinly sliced to serve
Korean chilli flakes (gochugaru) or mild chilli flakes
head soft lettuce (butterhead or green leaf), leaves separated
short-grain white rice, cooked to pack instructions without salt

steps.title: Firm up and slice
steps.text: Place the beef on the plate in the freezer for 40-60 min until firm but not frozen solid. Slice it across the grain as thinly as you can, aiming for 2-3 mm. Partly frozen meat holds its shape under the knife, and cutting across the grain keeps each slice tender.

steps.title: Blend the marinade
steps.text: Blend the pear, onion, garlic and ginger until smooth, then stir in the marinade soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil and pepper. Toss with the beef in the bowl, cover and refrigerate for 1-8 h. Enzymes in the pear soften the meat, but beyond 8 h the texture turns mushy.

steps.title: Stir the dipping sauce
steps.text: Mix the chilli flakes, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, rice vinegar, garlic and water in the small bowl. Resting while the beef cooks gives the chilli time to colour the sauce and soften.

steps.title: Sear in batches
steps.text: Heat the pan over high heat until smoking and add a little oil. Lift a third of the beef from the marinade, let the excess drip away and spread it in a single layer; cook for 2-3 min, turning, until browned at the edges and cooked through with clear juices (63°C if you probe a thicker piece). Small batches keep the pan hot enough to caramelise the sugars instead of stewing the meat.

steps.title: Add spring onions
steps.text: Toss in a third of the spring-onion lengths for the final 30 s of each batch so they wilt but stay bright. Wipe out any burnt marinade before the next batch, and discard any leftover marinade.

steps.title: Wrap and serve
steps.text: Scatter the beef with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion. Serve with the rice, lettuce leaves for wrapping and the chilli dipping sauce.

tips: A common mistake is piling all the beef into the pan at once; it releases liquid and boils, so cook in thirds.
Check the soy sauce label, as some brands contain alcohol.
Do not leave the beef in the marinade longer than 8 h, or the pear will make it soft and pasty.
Let the excess marinade drip off before cooking, since the sugars burn easily on a very hot pan.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate the beef for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan until piping hot (74°C); keep the lettuce and dipping sauce separate.
